fall_armyworm.description: A devastating pest of maize and other cereals in East Africa. Larvae feed on leaves, causing windowpane damage and characteristic ragged holes. Can cause 20-100% yield loss if untreated.
fall_armyworm.lowManagement: Monitor field every 3 days. Document egg masses and young larvae. Maintain field hygiene by removing crop residues. Encourage natural enemies (parasitoid wasps, predatory beetles).
fall_armyworm.moderateManagement: Apply biological control agents (Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki). Use neem-based botanical insecticides. Consider spot treatment of affected areas. Increase scouting to daily monitoring.
fall_armyworm.criticalManagement: Apply approved synthetic insecticides (Emamectin benzoate, Spinetoram) following label instructions. Treat entire field. Implement 7-day re-scouting. Consider crop rotation. Notify extension officer for area-wide management.

pesticides.name: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG
pesticides.notes: Apply when larvae are small (1st-2nd instar). Best applied in early morning or late evening.

pesticides.name: Spinetoram 12% SC
pesticides.notes: Translaminar action. Effective against resistant populations.

pesticides.name: Chlorantraniliprole 20% SC
pesticides.notes: Long residual activity. Apply at early infestation.

biologicalControls: Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki (Bt) - spray at 1-2kg/ha
Trichogramma egg parasitoids - release 50,000-100,000 per hectare
Nuclear polyhedrosis virus (NPV) - for heavy infestations

stalk_borer.displayName: Maize Stalk Borer (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus)
stalk_borer.description: Larvae bore into maize stems and cobs, causing 'deadheart' symptoms. Infested plants show wilting of central leaves. Can cause 30-80% yield loss in severe infestations.
stalk_borer.lowManagement: Monitor for egg masses on lower leaf surfaces. Remove and destroy infested plants (deadhearts). Maintain field sanitation. Avoid late planting which increases infestation risk.
stalk_borer.moderateManagement: Apply Trichogramma egg parasitoids. Use neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) as botanical spray. Push-pull technology with Napier grass borders and Desmodium intercrops.
stalk_borer.criticalManagement: Apply Chlorantraniliprole or Lambda-cyhalothrin to whorl. Split application recommended. Implement area-wide management. Consider resistant varieties for next season.

pesticides.name: Chlorantraniliprole 20% SC
pesticides.notes: Apply into whorl when 50% of plants show fresh damage.

pesticides.name: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC
pesticides.notes: Contact and stomach poison. Apply early morning.

maize_streak_virus.description: Transmitted by leafhoppers (Cicadulina mbila). Symptoms include streaking of leaves (parallel chlorotic lines), stunting, and poor ear fill. Can cause total crop failure in susceptible varieties.
maize_streak_virus.lowManagement: Monitor for leafhopper vectors. Remove infected plants immediately. Use reflective mulches to repel vectors. Plant early to avoid peak vector populations.
maize_streak_virus.moderateManagement: Apply systemic insecticides to control leafhoppers (Imidacloprid seed treatment). Rogue out infected plants. Maintain weed-free field margins. Consider resistant varieties.
maize_streak_virus.criticalManagement: Destroy severely infected fields. Apply systemic insecticides. Implement area-wide vector management. Plant resistant varieties (e.g., WE2109, SC Duma 43). Delay replanting by 2 weeks.

pesticides.name: Thiamethoxam 25% WG
pesticides.notes: Systemic action. Apply at first sign of leafhoppers.

biologicalControls: Resistant maize varieties (WE2109, SC Duma 43, TMV 1)

bean_fly.description: Larvae tunnel into bean stems near soil level, causing swelling and stem splitting. Plants wilt and may die. Most damaging during early growth stages. Can cause 50-100% plant mortality.
bean_fly.lowManagement: Plant at recommended spacing to reduce humidity. Avoid overhead irrigation. Monitor for adult flies using yellow sticky traps. Remove and destroy infested plants.
bean_fly.moderateManagement: Apply neem-based insecticides to seedlings. Use systemic seed treatment (Imidacloprid). Intercrop with non-host crops (maize, sorghum). Apply diatomaceous earth around stems.
bean_fly.criticalManagement: Apply systemic insecticides (Thiamethoxam, Cyantraniliprole). Reseed destroyed areas with treated seed. Implement area-wide management. Consider resistant varieties.

pesticides.name: Thiamethoxam 25% WG
pesticides.notes: Systemic. Apply at first true leaf stage.

pesticides.name: Cyantraniliprole 20% SC
pesticides.notes: Translaminar and systemic. Effective against resistant populations.

aphids.description: Sap-sucking insects that colonize leaves and stems. Cause yellowing, curling, and stunting. Produce honeydew that promotes sooty mold. Can transmit viral diseases. Common on beans, maize, and vegetables.
aphids.lowManagement: Monitor undersides of leaves. Use strong water spray to dislodge colonies. Encourage natural enemies (ladybirds, lacewings, hoverflies). Plant trap crops (nasturtium).
aphids.moderateManagement: Apply neem oil or insecticidal soap. Release ladybird beetles or lacewing larvae. Use reflective mulches. Remove heavily infested leaves.
aphids.criticalManagement: Apply systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam). Implement area-wide management. Consider biological control augmentation. Check for resistance.

pesticides.name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL
pesticides.notes: Systemic action. Avoid spraying during flowering to protect pollinators.

pesticides.name: Thiamethoxam 25% WG
pesticides.notes: Systemic. Apply as foliar spray or drench.

blight.description: A group of diseases affecting beans and vegetables. Symptoms include water-soaked lesions, leaf spots, stem cankers, and wilting. Spread by rain splash, contaminated seed, and tools.
blight.lowManagement: Use certified disease-free seed. Practice crop rotation (3-4 years). Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove infected plant debris. Maintain good field drainage.
blight.moderateManagement: Apply copper-based bactericides (Copper hydroxide). Use resistant varieties. Increase plant spacing for air circulation. Apply Trichoderma-based biocontrol agents.
blight.criticalManagement: Apply copper + Mancozeb combination. Destroy severely infected fields. Implement area-wide disease management. Quarantine infected areas. Use resistant varieties for replanting.

pesticides.name: Copper hydroxide 77% WP
pesticides.notes: Preventive. Apply every 7-10 days in wet weather.

pesticides.name: Mancozeb 80% WP + Copper
pesticides.notes: Combination for bacterial and fungal blight.

biologicalControls: Trichoderma harzianum - seed treatment and soil drench
Resistant varieties (e.g., KAT B1, KAT B9 for beans)

desert_locusts.description: Migratory swarms can devastate crops over large areas. Adults and nymphs (hoppers) consume all green vegetation. A swarm can eat as much as 35,000 people in a day. Major threat in East Africa.
desert_locusts.lowManagement: Report sightings to FAO Desert Locust Watch. Monitor breeding areas. Protect key crops with netting. Harvest early if possible.
desert_locusts.moderateManagement: Apply biopesticide (Metarhizium acridum) to hopper bands. Use ultra-low volume (ULV) spraying of approved insecticides. Implement ground control operations. Coordinate with national locust control centers.
desert_locusts.criticalManagement: Aerial spraying of Fenitrothion or Malathion (ULV). Coordinate with FAO and national authorities. Protect food storage. Emergency crop insurance claims. Replant resilient varieties.

pesticides.name: Fenitrothion 96% ULV
pesticides.notes: For aerial application against adult swarms. Coordinate with authorities.

pesticides.name: Malathion 96% ULV
pesticides.notes: Aerial application. Less persistent than Fenitrothion.

biologicalControls: Metarhizium acridum (Green Muscle) - fungal biopesticide for hoppers
Early detection and hopper band destruction

leafminer.description: Larvae create serpentine mines in leaves, stems, and fruits of tomatoes and other solanaceous crops. Can cause 100% yield loss. Also attacks potatoes, eggplant, and peppers.
leafminer.lowManagement: Use pheromone traps for monitoring and mass trapping. Remove and destroy infested leaves. Use insect-proof netting on greenhouses. Maintain field hygiene.
leafminer.moderateManagement: Apply neem-based insecticides. Release Trichogramma parasitoids. Use Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki. Apply diatomaceous earth. Intercrop with non-host crops.
leafminer.criticalManagement: Apply Spinosad or Chlorantraniliprole. Implement area-wide management. Destroy heavily infested crops. Use resistant varieties. Consider biological control augmentation.

pesticides.name: Spinosad 24% SC
pesticides.notes: Effective against larvae. Safe for beneficial insects when dry.

biologicalControls: Pheromone traps (TUA lure) for mass trapping
